chapter: Leaving New York, jazz styles and religion
title: His Methodist church and declining to run its music
summary: Smith attends a Methodist church but refuses to run the choir because it would take his time like the road.

story.theme_name: Church, faith and religion in a musician's life
story.community_name: Church, faith and jazz: the sacred and the secular

blocks.x: Do you go to a church locally around here?
Yeah. A little church right down there on Carthon Street.
Methodist. Yeah, it's a Methodist church.
Is there good music in the church?

Yeah. They got a lady piano player and they got a bass player playing organ. They tried to get me to play organ. I'd play piano or ...(?).., but it would consume my time. You'd have to get the choir together, and then (?) and the pastor wants to (?) out of town, and he's going and making TV shows and all that kind of stuff, and you have to buy those uniforms...
You have all that in your local church?

Yeah. With different kinds of uniforms and whatnot, and playing on the radio and all that. And I love to go fishing in a relaxing time, and I had to make a living. See, we weren't going to get paid. I might get paid five or ten dollars for playing on the Sunday in the church. But making all these out-of-town dates and things like that... Uh-huh, I couldn't go for it.
It would be like being on the road as a Jazz musician.

Yeah. Same thing. Same thing. Yeah! Sometimes maybe you have a service at the church, and then you have to go somewhere and run a program at some other church way across town and all that. And I knew that wasn't going to fit with me, so I just jumped down. Now it's just an (??)ancient memory(?). Of course, they got me students down there.
